units.translation: (in Harpocration, s.v. μαλκίομεν [we are numb], p. 198, 1 Oxford edition)
Thus Hermann for έλαδίω [with the olive-wood?] (or ἑλλαδίω [with the Helladic?]) κεκμῆτι [worn out].
Driving with a numb, unwearied foot.
i.e. those who receive the blow of the spear unshaken, like anvils, as the scholiast explains.
Mardon, Tharybis, anvils of the spear,
The savor is to be understood as that of sacrificial victims.
a house without savor of burnt sacrifice: the one without fire and savor. Thus Aeschylus (fr. 422).
that strangers come with words to my hearing.
Yet not without boasting does he stand at the gates.
Thus Hermann for ἀκορεστάτοις [most insatiable], which in one copy was changed to ακορεστοτάτοις [most insatiable].
an evil tale of ruinous, insatiable fortune.
and from good fortune to sprout insatiable misery for the race.
the insatiable end of many healths.
to fare well is insatiable for all mortals.
and let insatiable faction raise a cry for the race over the stoning victim.
[But at line 266 μηνεῖται ἄκη [the remedies are revealed?] is corrupt from μηνιαῖ᾽ ἄχη [monthly griefs].]
hoping for a surgical remedy for my woes.
having done surgical and releasing remedies for these things.
for if he knows any further remedy for evils.
for the opener (for the toucher Scaliger) there is no remedy of bridal chambers.
there is a remedy for this.
for this is a remedy among mortals for many things.
Let the people take care to work out remedies together.
for there is no remedy in lamenting this man.
and in disorderly flight (thus from one copy for ἀκόσμως [disorderly]) every ship was rowed.
not disorderly, but with obedient mind.
(with imperfect ἤκουον [I was hearing], perfect ἀκήκοα [I have heard], aorist ἤκουσα [I heard], future middle ἀκούσομαι [I will hear])
where Euripides in Aristophanes' Frogs 1172 mocks the tautology of the words κλύειν ἀκοῦσαι [to hear to listen].
did you hear, or did you not hear?
do not, hearing openly, hear too much.
a deed — fine to hear and to tell to those who are drunk.
these things are fears for me to see, but for you to hear.
and he immediately, when he heard.
and on this mound of the tomb I proclaim to my father to hear, to listen,
listen, such are the laments on your behalf.
hear, as I spoke about my own life.
and I wait to hear how the contest will be decided.
as he will hear (ἀκούση [he may hear] M).
I have heard, and you may speak.
